a01.heading: The Assembly
a01.plain: Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī, at Jeta Grove in the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty monks. All were great arhats, well known to everyone.
a01.commentary: Every sutra begins with "Thus have I heard," meaning that after the Buddha's passing, Venerable Ānanda passed it on as he heard it. The park of Anāthapiṇḍada is also known as Jetavana Monastery.

a02.heading: The Assembly
a02.plain: They were great disciples such as the elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Cūḍapanthaka, Nanda, Ānanda, Rāhula, Gavāṃpati, Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja, Kālodāyin, Mahākapphiṇa, Vakkula and Aniruddha.
a02.commentary: Sixteen of the Buddha's renowned disciples are named. The listener of this sutra is Śāriputra, foremost in wisdom.

a03.heading: The Assembly
a03.plain: With them were many great bodhisattvas, such as Mañjuśrī, Prince of the Dharma, Ajita Bodhisattva, Gandhahastin Bodhisattva and Nityodyukta Bodhisattva, and countless heavenly beings led by Śakra.
a03.commentary: Ajita is Maitreya Bodhisattva; Śakra is the god Indra. This shows that monks, bodhisattvas and heavenly beings had all gathered.

a04.heading: The Land of Bliss
a04.plain: Then the Buddha said to the elder Śāriputra: "West of here, beyond a hundred thousand million Buddha-lands, there is a world called Bliss. In that land there is a Buddha named Amitābha, who is teaching the Dharma right now."
a04.commentary: This is a sutra the Buddha taught on his own, without anyone asking.

a05.heading: The Land of Bliss
a05.plain: Śāriputra, why is that land called Bliss? The beings of that land suffer no pain at all and enjoy only happiness. That is why it is called Bliss.
a05.commentary: The Korean name means "utmost happiness." The Sanskrit name Sukhāvatī means "the place where happiness is."

a06.heading: Adornments of the Land of Bliss
a06.plain: Again, Śāriputra, the Land of Bliss is surrounded by seven rows of railings, seven layers of nets and seven rows of trees, all made of the four treasures. That is why it is called Bliss.
a06.commentary: The four treasures are gold, silver, lapis lazuli and crystal. "Sevenfold" expresses completeness and abundance.

a07.heading: Adornments of the Land of Bliss
a07.plain: Again, Śāriputra, in the Land of Bliss there are ponds of the seven treasures, filled with water of the eight virtues, their beds spread with golden sand. The steps on all four sides are made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli and crystal, and the pavilions above are adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, mother-of-pearl, red pearls and agate. The lotuses in the ponds are as large as cartwheels: blue ones give blue light, yellow ones yellow light, red ones red light, white ones white light, subtle, fragrant and pure. Śāriputra, the Land of Bliss is complete with such merit and adornment.
a07.commentary: Water of the eight virtues is clear, cool, sweet, soft, moistening, soothing, quenching and nourishing.

a08.heading: Adornments of the Land of Bliss
a08.plain: Again, Śāriputra, in that Buddha-land heavenly music always plays and the ground is gold. Six times each day and night, māndārava flowers rain down from the sky. Each clear morning the beings of that land fill the folds of their robes with lovely flowers and offer them to a hundred thousand million Buddhas in other worlds. At mealtime they return to their own land, eat, and practice walking meditation. Śāriputra, the Land of Bliss is complete with such merit and adornment.
a08.commentary: Walking meditation is practice done by walking slowly back and forth in one place. Life in the Land of Bliss is itself offering and practice.

a09.heading: Birds That Sing the Dharma
a09.plain: Moreover, Śāriputra, that land always has wondrous birds of many colors: white cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynas, kalaviṅkas and two-headed birds. Six times each day and night these birds sing in harmonious, gentle voices. Their song proclaims teachings such as the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening and the noble eightfold path. Hearing it, the beings of that land all bring to mind the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha.
a09.commentary: Even birdsong teaches practice (part of the thirty-seven aids to awakening). Recollecting the Buddha, Dharma and Sangha means keeping the Three Jewels always in mind.

a10.heading: Birds That Sing the Dharma
a10.plain: Śāriputra, do not think these birds were born as the result of wrongdoing. Why? Because in that Buddha-land there are no three evil paths. Not even the name of the three evil paths exists there, let alone the reality. These birds were all created by Amitābha Buddha's transformation, to spread the sound of the Dharma.
a10.commentary: The three evil paths are the hells, hungry ghosts and animals. The birds of the Pure Land are not animals but appear through the Buddha's skillful means.

a11.heading: Birds That Sing the Dharma
a11.plain: Śāriputra, when a gentle breeze in that Buddha-land stirs the rows of jewel trees and jewel nets, they give a subtle sound, like a hundred thousand instruments playing at once. Whoever hears it naturally brings to mind the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha. Śāriputra, that Buddha-land is complete with such merit and adornment.
a11.commentary: Not only the birds but the wind and trees, everything there awakens one to the Dharma.

a12.heading: The Name Amitābha
a12.plain: Śāriputra, what do you think? Why is that Buddha called Amitābha? Śāriputra, that Buddha's light is boundless and shines unhindered on the lands of the ten directions; that is why he is called Amitābha. And Śāriputra, the life of that Buddha and of his people lasts for boundless, endless asaṃkhyeya kalpas; that is why he is called Amitāyus. Śāriputra, ten kalpas have passed since Amitābha became a Buddha.
a12.commentary: Amita means "immeasurable." The name holds both meanings: Boundless Light (Amitābha) and Boundless Life (Amitāyus).

a13.heading: The Holy Ones of the Land of Bliss
a13.plain: Again, Śāriputra, that Buddha has boundless, endless śrāvaka disciples, all arhats, more than can be counted. So too with the bodhisattvas. Śāriputra, that Buddha-land is complete with such merit and adornment.
a13.commentary: Śrāvakas are disciples who attain awakening by hearing the Buddha's teaching.

a14.heading: The Holy Ones of the Land of Bliss
a14.plain: Again, Śāriputra, the beings born in the Land of Bliss never turn back, and many of them will become Buddhas after just one more life. Their number is so great it cannot be counted; it can only be called boundless, endless asaṃkhyeyas.
a14.commentary: A bodhisattva "one life from Buddhahood" is in the position to become a Buddha in the next life. Maitreya Bodhisattva is the best-known example.

a15.heading: Vow to Be Born There
a15.plain: Śāriputra, beings who hear this should vow to be born in that land. Why? Because there they can gather in one place with such excellent people. Śāriputra, one cannot be born in that land with only small roots of goodness, merit and virtue.
a15.commentary: "Small roots of goodness are not enough" is said to stress the single-minded recitation in the next verse.

a16.heading: Recitation with an Undistracted Mind
a16.plain: Śāriputra, if a good man or good woman hears of Amitābha Buddha and holds firmly to his name, for one day, two days, three, four, five, six or seven days, with a single, undistracted mind, then when that person's life is ending, Amitābha Buddha and the holy assembly will appear before them. At the end, their mind will not be confused, and they will at once be reborn in Amitābha Buddha's Land of Bliss.
a16.commentary: The key passage of this sutra. "Holding the name with an undistracted mind" is the basis of reciting "Namo Amitābha Buddha."

a17.heading: Recitation with an Undistracted Mind
a17.plain: Śāriputra, because I see this benefit, I say these words. Beings who hear this teaching should vow to be born in that land.
a17.commentary: The Buddha himself vouches for the benefit and urges the vow.

a18.heading: The Buddhas of the East Bear Witness
a18.plain: Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable merit of Amitābha Buddha, in the east too there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Akṣobhya Buddha, Sumeru Sign Buddha, Great Sumeru Buddha, Sumeru Light Buddha and Wondrous Sound Buddha. Each in his own land extends his broad, long tongue, covering the whole great trichiliocosm, and speaks these sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra, Praised for Inconceivable Merit and Protected by All Buddhas."
a18.commentary: The broad, long tongue is a sign that a Buddha never lies. The Buddhas of the six directions bear witness to this sutra in turn. The first Buddha of the east, Akṣobhya, means "the Unshakable"; he is the Buddha of the eastern world of Abhirati. In Korean chanting the Buddhas' names are read aloud in their traditional pronunciation rather than translated, as names of reverence.

a19.heading: The Buddhas of the South Bear Witness
a19.plain: Śāriputra, in the southern worlds there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Sun-Moon Lamp Buddha, Renowned Light Buddha, Great Blazing Shoulders Buddha, Sumeru Lamp Buddha and Boundless Vigor Buddha. Each covers the great trichiliocosm with his broad, long tongue and speaks sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra."
a19.commentary: The same form repeats across all six directions.

a20.heading: The Buddhas of the West Bear Witness
a20.plain: Śāriputra, in the western worlds there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Boundless Life Buddha, Boundless Signs Buddha, Boundless Banner Buddha, Great Light Buddha, Great Brightness Buddha, Jewel Sign Buddha and Pure Light Buddha. Each covers the great trichiliocosm with his broad, long tongue and speaks sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra."
a20.commentary: The first Buddha of the west, Boundless Life Buddha, is Amitābha himself.

a21.heading: The Buddhas of the North Bear Witness
a21.plain: Śāriputra, in the northern worlds there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Blazing Shoulders Buddha, Most Excellent Sound Buddha, Hard to Obstruct Buddha, Sunrise Buddha and Net Brightness Buddha. Each covers the great trichiliocosm with his broad, long tongue and speaks sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra."

a22.heading: The Buddhas Below Bear Witness
a22.plain: Śāriputra, in the worlds below there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Lion Buddha, Renown Buddha, Famous Light Buddha, Dharma Buddha, Dharma Banner Buddha and Dharma Holder Buddha. Each covers the great trichiliocosm with his broad, long tongue and speaks sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra."

a23.heading: The Buddhas Above Bear Witness
a23.plain: Śāriputra, in the worlds above there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, such as Brahma Voice Buddha, King of Constellations Buddha, Superior Fragrance Buddha, Fragrant Light Buddha, Great Blazing Shoulders Buddha, Body Adorned with Many-Colored Jewel Flowers Buddha, Sāla Tree King Buddha, Jewel Flower Virtue Buddha, Seeing All Meanings Buddha and Like Mount Sumeru Buddha. Each covers the great trichiliocosm with his broad, long tongue and speaks sincere words: "All you beings should believe in this sutra."

a24.heading: The Sutra Protected by All Buddhas
a24.plain: Śāriputra, what do you think? Why is this called the Sutra Protected by All Buddhas? Śāriputra, if a good man or good woman hears this sutra and holds it, or hears the names of these Buddhas, all the Buddhas together protect and keep them in mind, and they will never turn back from supreme, perfect awakening. Therefore, Śāriputra, all of you should believe and accept my words and the words of all the Buddhas.
a24.commentary: Anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi means "supreme, right and equal awakening": the awakening of a Buddha.

a25.heading: The Merit of the Vow
a25.plain: Śāriputra, those who have already vowed, are now vowing, or will vow to be born in Amitābha Buddha's land will never turn back from supreme, perfect awakening. They have already been born there, are being born there now, or will be born there. Therefore, Śāriputra, good men and good women who have faith should vow to be born in that land.
a25.commentary: By naming vows of past, present and future, it shows that it is never too late to vow.

a26.heading: Śākyamuni Buddha's Difficult Deed
a26.plain: Śāriputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable merit of the Buddhas, those Buddhas also praise my inconceivable merit, saying: "Śākyamuni Buddha has done something very difficult and rare. In the Sahā world, an evil age of the five turbidities (a turbid age, turbid views, turbid afflictions, turbid beings and turbid lifespans), he attained supreme, perfect awakening and, for all beings, taught this Dharma that the whole world finds hard to believe."
a26.commentary: The five turbidities are five kinds of murkiness of a degenerate age. The praise is that awakening and teaching in such a world is the hardest thing of all.

a27.heading: Śākyamuni Buddha's Difficult Deed
a27.plain: Śāriputra, know that in this evil age of the five turbidities I did this difficult thing: I attained supreme, perfect awakening and taught this hard-to-believe Dharma for the whole world. This is truly difficult.
a27.commentary: "The hard-to-believe Dharma" is interpreted as the teaching that one reaches the Land of Bliss through the easy practice of calling the Buddha's name.

a28.heading: Conclusion
a28.plain: When the Buddha had finished teaching this sutra, Śāriputra, the monks, and all the heavenly beings, humans and asuras of the world heard what the Buddha said, rejoiced, believed and accepted it, bowed and departed.
a28.commentary: The closing section of the sutra. Most sutras end like this, with the assembly joyfully accepting the teaching.

amitabha.definition: The Buddha of the Western Land of Bliss: the Buddha of boundless light (Amitābha) and boundless life (Amitāyus).

sukhavati.definition: Sukhāvatī, Amitābha's Western Pure Land: a world with no suffering, only happiness, and ideal for practice.

sariputra.definition: Foremost in wisdom among the Buddha's disciples. The same Śāriputra as in the Heart Sutra.

arhat.definition: A saint who has cut off all afflictions and is no longer reborn. The word means "worthy of offerings."

kalpa.definition: An immeasurably long span of time. Asaṃkhyeya means "a number that cannot be counted."

avaivartika.definition: The stage of never again turning back on the path to awakening.

nembutsu.definition: Bringing the Buddha to mind, especially the practice of gathering the mind by calling "Namo Amitābha Buddha."

anuttara.definition: Supreme, right and equal awakening: the complete awakening of a Buddha.

saha.definition: "The world of endurance": the world we live in, where Śākyamuni Buddha teaches.

samadhi-wings.definition: Thirty-seven practices that lead to awakening, including the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening and the noble eightfold path.
